documents.title: Preoperative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PREOPERATIVE MEDICAL EVALUATION
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy, 2/6/2026, general surgery. General anesthesia planned.

History: cholangitis from a common duct stone 12/2025 treated with ERCP, sphincterotomy and extraction; long history of gallstones with colic. No pain since discharge. T2DM on metformin and glipizide, HTN on lisinopril, obesity, on atorvastatin.
Prior anesthesia: T&A as a child, C-section 1994 - no problems she knows of. No family history of anesthesia reactions.
Functional capacity: walks 30 min, climbs 2 flights without stopping, well over 4 METs. No chest pain, dyspnea, orthopnea, palpitations or syncope. No snoring or daytime sleepiness she has noticed.
NKDA. Former smoker.

Exam: vitals as charted. Airway: normal mouth opening, neck full range. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema.

ECG today: normal sinus rhythm, normal intervals, no conduction abnormality.

Assessment: low risk for a low-risk procedure. No further cardiac testing needed. Medically optimized.

Periop plan:
- Metformin: hold the morning of surgery, resume when eating.
- Glipizide: hold the morning of surgery, resume when eating normally.
- Lisinopril: hold the morning of surgery, resume the next day if BP allows.
- Atorvastatin: continue.
- Check sugar the morning of surgery.
CBC, BMP and A1c drawn today; will forward with this note and the ECG to the surgery office.

documents.title: Pre-op labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra, your pre-op blood count and chemistry are normal and your ECG was normal. The A1c came back a little higher at 7.9 - not surprising after being so sick in December, and fine for surgery. We'll recheck it in the spring. I faxed everything to the surgeon's office this morning, so you're all set for 2/6. Remember: no metformin, glipizide or lisinopril the morning of surgery. Good luck!

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 02/06/2026
Preoperative diagnosis: symptomatic cholelithiasis, status post ERCP for choledocholithiasis with cholangitis.
Postoperative diagnosis: same.
Procedure: laparoscopic cholecystectomy.
Anesthesia: general endotracheal.
EBL: minimal. Specimen: gallbladder to pathology. Complications: intraoperative bradycardia with insufflation, resolved (see below).

Description: After induction and intubation the abdomen was prepped and draped. Periumbilical access with a Hasson technique, CO2 pneumoperitoneum established, three additional ports placed under direct vision. About thirty minutes into the case, during insufflation, anesthesia called a sudden fall in heart rate to 40 with blood pressure 110/70; she was otherwise stable and there had been no technical difficulty. The abdomen was desufflated and atropine 0.5 mg IV given by anesthesia, with heart rate recovering to the 70s within about a minute. After a brief pause, pneumoperitoneum was re-established slowly at a lower pressure without recurrence. The gallbladder was retracted, the critical view of safety obtained, and the cystic duct and artery clipped and divided. The gallbladder was removed from the liver bed with cautery and extracted in a bag. Hemostasis confirmed. Ports removed under vision, fascia closed at the umbilicus, skin closed with absorbable suture.

Impression: uncomplicated laparoscopic cholecystectomy apart from vagal bradycardia from the pneumoperitoneum, which responded promptly.
Plan: overnight observation on telemetry given the intraoperative bradycardia.

documents.title: Surgical Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
SHORT STAY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 02/06/2026 for laparoscopic cholecystectomy; discharged 02/07/2026.

Intraoperative vagal bradycardia during CO2 insufflation, treated with desufflation and atropine; procedure completed. Preoperative ECG had been normal sinus rhythm. Overnight telemetry: sinus rhythm throughout, no further bradycardia. Tolerated diet, ambulating, pain controlled with oral medicines. Sore throat from the breathing tube noted on the morning of discharge.

Discharge medications: oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 mg 1 tab q6h prn severe pain, #10; acetaminophen 1000 mg q8h prn (do not combine above 3 g/day total acetaminophen). Resume metformin, glipizide, lisinopril and atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: surgery clinic in 2 weeks. Pathology pending at discharge.

documents.title: Pathology Result Received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Gallbladder pathology from 2/6 surgery received from the hospital and filed: gallstones, no dysplasia or malignancy. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Hoarseness After Surgery
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt called. Gallbladder out Friday; incisions fine, pain mild, only took 2 of the oxycodone. Her voice has been hoarse and her throat scratchy since she woke up from anesthesia, maybe a little worse yesterday after a long phone call. Swallowing OK, no trouble breathing, no noisy breathing, no fever, no cough. Advised rest the voice, warm fluids. She would like to be seen since her job is mostly on the phone. Booked Thu 2/12 with PCP. ED for any breathing difficulty.

documents.title: Office Visit - Hoarseness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6 days s/p lap chole (2/6, general ET anesthesia). Op note and discharge summary reviewed: bradycardia to 40 with insufflation, reversed with desufflation and atropine, case completed, no recurrence overnight on tele.

Hoarse since extubation with a raw throat. Not worse, not better. Swallowing solids and liquids fine. No stridor, dyspnea, cough, fever. No palpitations, lightheadedness or fainting since surgery. Incisions sore but OK. Off the oxycodone, using acetaminophen once a day.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Voice hoarse, breathy. Oropharynx without exudate. No neck swelling or tenderness, no nodes. No stridor. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Port sites clean, dry, no erythema.

A/P
1. Acute laryngitis - post-intubation. Voice rest (no whispering), humidifier, fluids, avoid throat clearing. Should settle over 1-2 weeks. If still hoarse at 3 weeks, call and we'll get ENT to look.
2. Vagal bradycardia from pneumoperitoneum - single intraoperative event, normal preop ECG, no symptoms since; resolved, nothing further needed.
3. Post-op - healing well, surgery f/u 2/20.
Work note given for 2 days of reduced phone duties.

documents.title: General Surgery Postoperative Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Dear Doctor,

Ms. Wojcik was seen on 02/20/2026, two weeks after her laparoscopic cholecystectomy. She is eating a normal diet without pain, bowels are regular, and she has no fever. Her voice is improving. Port sites are healed with no hernia or infection.

Pathology showed gallstones without dysplasia or malignancy, which we reviewed with her.

She may return to all activity. No routine surgical follow-up is needed; we would be glad to see her again if any problem arises. Medications unchanged: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.

Thank you for referring her.

General Surgery

documents.title: Emergency Department Physician Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 03/07/2026 (Saturday)

CC: Severe right upper abdominal pain, fever, yellow skin.

HPI: 55F, laparoscopic cholecystectomy 2/6/2026, ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone removal 12/2025 for cholangitis, T2DM, HTN. Since last night: severe RUQ pain, fevers, nausea and several episodes of vomiting, yellow skin this morning. Over the past hour in the department she has become more confused and drowsy.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS. NKDA.

Exam: T 38.9 C (102 F), BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22. Jaundiced, in obvious distress, drowsy and intermittently confused. Marked RUQ tenderness. Port sites healed. Lungs clear.

Labs: WBC 18.0, Hgb 12.5, plt 250. T bili 5.2, direct 3.8, alk phos 210, AST 80, ALT 75. Amylase 300, lipase 900. Blood cultures x2.
Ultrasound: CBD stone with intrahepatic ductal dilation; gallbladder absent.

Course: IV fluid boluses with BP persistently low; norepinephrine started. IV piperacillin-tazobactam after cultures. Critical care and GI consulted.

Impression: recurrent choledocholithiasis with acute cholangitis; septic shock.
Disposition: ICU.

documents.title: ERCP Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY
Date of procedure: 03/08/2026, ICU patient, performed under general anesthesia.
Indication: cholangitis with septic shock; CBD stone on ultrasound; prior sphincterotomy 12/2025; cholecystectomy 2/2026.

Prior sphincterotomy noted and patent. Deep biliary cannulation. Cholangiogram: dilated common bile duct with a single filling defect in the distal duct and dilated intrahepatic ducts. Cystic duct stump clips in good position, no leak. Balloon sweeps removed one stone with sludge and purulent bile. Occlusion cholangiogram: no residual filling defects, good drainage.

Impression: retained/recurrent common bile duct stone, cleared.
Recommendations: complete antibiotics; GI clinic follow-up in about 6 weeks with liver tests.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 03/07/2026 (ICU 03/07-03/10), discharged 03/13/2026.

Diagnoses: septic shock due to acute cholangitis; recurrent choledocholithiasis (retained common duct stone) one month after cholecystectomy. Amylase and lipase elevation on arrival with the stone impacted in the distal duct, trending down after drainage.

Course: Hypotensive despite fluid resuscitation; norepinephrine for about 24 hours in the ICU. IV piperacillin-tazobactam. ERCP 03/08 with balloon extraction of a distal duct stone; duct clear. Off norepinephrine 03/09, mentation back to baseline the same day. Transferred to the floor 03/10. Bilirubin, liver enzymes and lipase falling daily; tolerating a low-fat diet. Blood cultures without growth. Metformin and glipizide held in the ICU with insulin; resumed 03/12 when eating normally and kidney function normal.

Discharge medications:
- Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg BID through 03/16 to complete the course.
- Metformin 1000 mg BID, glipizide 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg qHS - continue.
- Lisinopril 10 mg - HOLD until seen by PCP, given recent shock; blood pressure normal off it in hospital.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (liver tests, CBC, BMP, lipase, BP check and decision on lisinopril). GI clinic in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Transition of Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hospital records received this morning, reviewed. Called pt. Home since Friday. Very tired, sleeping a lot, appetite slowly coming back. No fever, no pain, color normal. Last antibiotic dose tonight. Not taking lisinopril per hospital instructions; taking metformin, glipizide, atorvastatin. Fasting sugars ok, no lows. Has a home cuff - asked her to check BP daily and bring the readings. Booked with PCP Thu 3/19, labs same day. District has her out through next week. ED for fever, pain, jaundice or confusion.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hospital follow-up, high complexity. ED record, ERCP report and discharge summary reviewed.

Summary: 3/7-3/13 admission (ICU 3 days) for septic shock from acute cholangitis due to a retained common duct stone, a month after lap chole. Needed norepinephrine about a day. ERCP 3/8 with balloon extraction, duct clear. Lipase was 900 on arrival with the stone at the ampulla, falling with drainage. Cultures negative. Finished amox-clav 3/16.

Now: tired but improving each day, walking around the block. No pain, fever, chills, vomiting. Eating small meals. Urine and stool normal color. Thinking clear - remembers almost nothing of the first day. Home BP readings since discharge running higher than her usual. Sugars fine.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, glipizide 5, atorvastatin 20. Lisinopril on hold since discharge.

Exam: tired-appearing but well. Afebrile. BP as charted, above goal. Sclerae anicteric. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, port sites healed. No edema. Alert, oriented, conversing normally.

A/P
1. Septic shock from cholangitis - resolved. Off pressors since 3/9, antibiotics complete.
2. Choledocholithiasis with cholangitis (retained stone) - cleared at ERCP, clinically resolved. Repeat LFTs, lipase, CBC today. GI clinic 4/21.
3. HTN - BP back up off lisinopril, kidney function normal at discharge. Restart lisinopril 10 daily; BMP today and keep home log.
4. T2DM - back on metformin/glipizide, no lows; A1c at May visit.
She asked whether this could happen again - explained a further duct stone is possible but much less likely now that the gallbladder is out and the duct has been cleared twice; warning signs reviewed. Return to work note for 3/30.

documents.title: Hospital follow-up labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sandra - good news. Your liver tests, lipase and white count are all back to normal, and your kidney function and potassium are fine, so it's safe to be back on the lisinopril. Keep checking your blood pressure at home and send me a few readings in a couple of weeks. Rest up.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Clinic Letter
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
GASTROENTEROLOGY CLINIC
Date of visit: 04/21/2026

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Wojcik in follow-up after her ERCP of 03/08/2026, when a retained distal common bile duct stone was cleared during an admission for cholangitis with septic shock. This followed an earlier ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction in 12/2025 and laparoscopic cholecystectomy in 02/2026.

She has been well since discharge with no abdominal pain, fever, jaundice, nausea or change in stool or urine color. She is back at work full time.

Medications: metformin, glipizide, lisinopril, atorvastatin. NKDA.
Exam: well appearing, anicteric. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Liver tests drawn today are normal.

Impression: choledocholithiasis, cleared, now status post cholecystectomy with a patent sphincterotomy.
Plan: no further ERCP or imaging planned. She knows to seek care urgently for pain, fever or jaundice, and we would be happy to see her again if symptoms recur.

Sincerely,
Gastroenterology

GI letter 4/21: LFTs normal, no further ERCP planned. Back on lisinopril since 3/19 - home BPs back to her usual range. Sugars stable, no lows. Taking all meds.

2. HTN - back at goal on lisinopril 10.
3. S/p cholecystectomy, choledocholithiasis x2 cleared - doing well, nothing further.
